brief.headline: The load-bearing wall of the aluminium bull case came under direct attack over the weekend: Trump cancelled the planned strike on Iran, said the perimeters of a deal are agreed and claimed an immediate and complete opening of the Strait of Hormuz - Brent fell 4.61% to $83.88 and European gas 4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on Monday - while the LME board itself is frozen on Friday's 31-Jul official until the 13:20 ring.
bullets: WHAT MOVED - AND IT WAS NOT THE LME. There is no new official to report: no exchange session runs at the weekend and Monday's ring has not taken place at this compile, so cash $3,196.00, 3M $3,179.00, the +$17.00 backwardation and 264,400 t of stock all still date from 31-Jul. What moved is the risk premium underneath them. Trump cancelled a planned military strike on Iran late on Saturday, said the 'perimeters of a deal' had been agreed after Saudi, UAE and Iranian pressure for diplomacy, and claimed the deal delivers an immediate, complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz, with talks starting Monday afternoon. Brent fell 4.61% to $83.88 and Dutch TTF gas 4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on the news.

WHY IT MATTERS - THE GULF PREMIUM IS THE SINGLE LARGEST PILLAR OF THE PRICE. The precedent is unambiguous and it comes from the official record, not from commentary: on the 17-Jun 60-day ceasefire the official cash fell from $3,855.00 on 02-Jun to $3,061.50 in early July, a 20.6% drawdown, and June's monthly mean of $3,458.64 gave way to July's $3,155.98 (-8.7%). TWO THINGS CUT THE OTHER WAY. First, this is announced, not signed - talks only BEGIN Monday afternoon and the 01-Aug tanker strike near Lima, Oman is 48 hours old. Second, Gulf physical supply cannot return on a headline: EGA had 89 of 1,262 pots back in operation at 02-Jul, and Alba's Lines 1-3, shut on 15-Mar and equal to 19% of a 1,623,000 t/y smelter, have no publicly disclosed restart date. Lower oil also cuts the COST floor - petroleum coke feeds the prebaked anode - so de-escalation lowers the price and the cost line together.

THE 48 HOURS - THE DEMAND CROSS-CHECK CAME BACK SPLIT, AND JAPAN INTERVENED. The private RatingDog (ex-Caixin) July manufacturing PMI printed 50.9, a four-month low from 51.7 and below the 51.5 consensus, but still IN EXPANSION - directly contradicting the official NBS gauge at 49.2. New orders rose for a 14th month and foreign sales rose for the first time in three. The rest of Asia confirmed the private read: Korea 53.1, Taiwan 55.1, Vietnam 52.9, all expanding with export orders improving. Separately Japan and the US confirmed their first JOINT yen-buying intervention since 2011; the yen has firmed about 5% in three sessions to 156.44, which raises the local-currency cost of dollar metal just as Q4 CIF Japan talks approach.

WHAT TO WATCH. Monday's 13:20 official is now doubly informative - the first August print AND the first official struck after the de-escalation headline. Three specific tests: whether the +$17.00 backwardation holds, rebuilds or flips to contango; whether stock breaks 260,000 t after 23 consecutive draws to a century low; and whether Hormuz transit counts actually recover from about ten commodity vessels on Friday against more than 100 before the war. Alba reports Q2-2026 on Tuesday 04-Aug - the first Gulf producer P&L covering a full quarter of the Lines 1-3 shutdown.

The counter-evidence also still stands - exchange stock drew a further 1,900 t to a century low on the same session, so availability did not loosen even as the prompt premium halved. Monday's ring now tests the same spread against a SUPPLY-side headline pointing in the same bearish direction, which is a materially harder test than the first one.

lme.commentary: THE BOARD IS FROZEN AND THE MARKET IS NOT. No LME session took place on Saturday 01-Aug or Sunday 02-Aug, and Monday 03-Aug's 13:20-London ring has not yet run at this ~06:00 compile, so the 31-JULY-2026 OFFICIAL remains the latest published official in existence. Every LME figure on this board is therefore unchanged from the prior compile BY CONSTRUCTION, not by carry-forward of a stale read - the source was re-checked this run and confirms 31-Jul is still the operative session. The 31-Jul official stands at cash $3,196.00 (-$35.00, -1.08%), 3M $3,179.00 (-$8.00, -0.25%), a BACKWARDATION of +$17.00 down from +$44.00, and stock of 264,400 t (-1,900 t) - a fresh low this century after 23 consecutive published sessions of draws, -48.1% year-to-date. WHAT CHANGED IS THE INPUT, NOT THE OUTPUT. Over the weekend Trump cancelled a planned strike on Iran, said the perimeters of a deal had been agreed and claimed the deal opens the Strait of Hormuz; Brent fell 4.61% and Dutch TTF gas 4.23% on Monday. Monday's 13:20 ring is therefore the first official to price a supply-risk reversal, and it arrives with the prompt premium already halved by Friday's demand shock. THE TWO FORCES NOW POINT THE SAME WAY, which is why the +$17.00 spread is the number to watch: it has already failed one test, and a second bearish input lands on it immediately. AGAINST THAT, the inventory evidence is untouched - 264,400 t of exchange stock does not rebuild because talks are scheduled, EGA had 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul, and Alba's Lines 1-3 have been down since 15-Mar. The bull case has lost its narrative but not yet its physical base. SPREAD CONVENTION: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION (nearby tightness); cash below 3M is CONTANGO.

regional.basis: Q3-2026 SETTLED at $395/t CIF Japan (S&P Global Platts, assessed 06-Jul-2026) - an 11-year high (prior peak Q3-2014 $404/t), +11.9-12.9% q/q versus Q2's $350-353, built from 10 trades at $395/t for a combined minimum 15,500 t/month, July-September loading. QUARTERLY BASIS: this does not re-price daily and no fresher public print exists at this 03-Aug refresh; a dedicated search for Q4-2026 offers, talks coverage or settlement returned nothing public. Talks are expected to open around late August. THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP MOVED AGAINST SELLERS OVER THIS WEEKEND, having moved for them over the previous one. FOR the buyers: Trump cancelled the planned Iran strike on 01-Aug and claims a deal opening the Strait of Hormuz, which attacks the scarcity narrative underneath an 11-year-high premium; Japan and the US confirmed their first JOINT yen intervention since 2011 and the yen has firmed roughly 5% in three sessions to 156.44, mechanically raising the local-currency cost of dollar metal; the official China PMI is in contraction at 49.2; and the LME backwardation has halved to +$17.00. FOR the sellers: exchange stock is at a century low of 264,400 t, EGA had only 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul, and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) have been down since 15-Mar with no public restart date. AL Circle's 24-Jul review notes the CIF Japan premium rose 127% quarter-on-quarter in early 2026 - context for why buyers resisted producer offers of $440-480.

Platts CIF Japan spot P1020/P1020A $370/t over LME cash, assessed 06-Jul-2026. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - the freshest publicly retrievable mark, now 28 days old at this 03-Aug refresh; it is carried at its assessment date and is NOT a current-session value. No daily move should be inferred. Against the 31-Jul cash official of $3,196.00 an all-in Japanese delivered equivalent computes to roughly $3,566/t, of which the premium is about 10.4%. THE FX LEG IS THE LIVE VARIABLE THIS RUN: USD/JPY is 156.44 on Monday 03-Aug after Japan's Ministry of Finance and the US Treasury confirmed a coordinated yen-buying intervention - the first joint action since 2011 - with Tokyo warning it stands ready to act again. The yen has gained about 5% in three sessions from 163.4 a week earlier. For a Japanese buyer paying in yen, that is a direct reduction in the local-currency cost of the same dollar premium, and it cuts both ways: it improves affordability but it also removes one of the arguments producers used for a higher Q4 number.

European P1020A duty-unpaid in-warehouse Rotterdam, carried at its last public assessment. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT, not a daily mark - no fresher free public print is available at this 03-Aug refresh, so the value is held at its assessment date rather than implied to have moved. The duty-unpaid leg is the cleanest read on genuine European physical tightness because it excludes both the 6% EU import duty and the CBAM cost embedded in duty-paid assessments since January 2026. DISCLOSURE ON WHAT IS AND IS NOT PUBLIC: the duty-PAID Rotterdam assessment does have a post-6-Jul public print - Fastmarkets' 14-Jul-2026 pricing notice carries P1020A duty-paid in-warehouse Rotterdam at $510-540/t - but the duty-UNPAID series (MB-AL-0346) has no publicly retrievable figure dated after early March 2026, so it is NOT updated from the duty-paid read. The regional backdrop turned two-sided over the weekend: European gas fell 4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on the strike cancellation, which improves restart economics at the margin, while the Suez routing that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam remains impaired by the Bab al Mandeb disruption.

6063 extrusion billet premium, in-warehouse duty-paid Rotterdam (Fastmarkets MB-AL-0002 basis), carried at its last public assessment date. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - not refreshed daily. Billet premiums carry the duty-paid structure plus the conversion spread over P1020, so they move with both metal availability and extruder order books. European extrusion demand remains the soft spot in the regional balance. THE ENERGY LEG IMPROVED THIS RUN: TTF gas fell 4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on Monday 03-Aug after the Iran strike was called off, from EUR 59.07 at the 31-Jul close - the first material downtick in a month that still ran roughly 36-37% higher. Hydro's Slovalco agreement with the Slovak government to resume 75,000 t from Q4-2026 remains the first concrete European restart of the cycle, and cheaper power is exactly the condition that would let others follow. EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, was still in force at the last public check (20-Jul).

Platts US Midwest transaction premium, carried at its 06-Jul-2026 assessment of roughly $2,380/t (about 108 c/lb) after $2,396/t on 03-Jul; no fresher free public print is retrievable at this 03-Aug refresh, so it is held at its assessment date and no daily move should be inferred. The US premium is overwhelmingly a TARIFF construct rather than a scarcity signal: at the 31-Jul cash of $3,196.00 the 50% Section 232 rate on aluminium articles is $1,598.00/t on its own. The rate was re-verified unchanged this run. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally allows companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) to import at HALF the applicable rate against expected output; no CBP guidance implementing that measure has been issued yet, and it is the main identified route by which the US premium could compress without any change to the headline tariff.

US Midwest duty-paid P1020A, carried at its last public assessment date - PERIODIC, not a daily mark, and not refreshed this run because no fresher free public print exists. This is the tariff-inflated delivered number and it is the row the tariff decomposition on this board matches against. DECOMPOSITION REFRESHED EVERY RUN: at the 31-Jul cash official of $3,196.00 the 50% Section 232 ad-valorem leg alone is $1,598.00/t, unchanged from the prior compile because the metal price is unchanged; the residual above that is the genuine physical/logistics component. Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs (15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members) run from 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 under Federal Register 2026-11314. Alcoa's Q2-2026 disclosure of roughly $35m of additional Section 232 cost on Canadian metal is the clearest public evidence that the tariff is a real cash cost to cross-border producers as well as a premium inflator.

drivers.text: THE WEEKEND REMOVED THE MARGINAL BUYER OF RISK: Trump cancelled the planned strike on Iran, said the perimeters of a deal are agreed and claimed an immediate and complete opening of the Strait of Hormuz, with talks starting Monday afternoon — Al Jazeera, NPR and Bloomberg all carry the same 02-Aug account: after Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Iran pressed for diplomacy, Trump called off a strike he had planned for the weekend, posted late on 01-Aug that the 'perimeters of a deal' had been reached, and framed the deal as delivering an immediate, complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Talks were scheduled to begin Monday afternoon. The market reaction is unambiguous in the energy complex - Brent -4.61% to $83.88 and Dutch TTF -4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh on 03-Aug - and every physical aluminium premium on this board has a Gulf-risk component that the same headline attacks. WHAT IS NOT YET SOURCEABLE: no aluminium-specific price assessment or news analysis dated 02-03 Aug has been published on the read-across, so the premium impact stated here is explicitly inference from the energy tape and the June precedent, not an assessed move. The June precedent is on the official record: on the 17-Jun 60-day ceasefire the LME official cash fell from $3,855.00 on 02-Jun to $3,061.50 in early July, -20.6%.
drivers.source: Al Jazeera - Trump cancels Iran strike, says deal perimeters reached (02-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Physical Gulf supply cannot return on a headline - EGA had 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3, 19% of a 1,623,000 t/y smelter, have been shut since 15-Mar with no public restart date — This is the strongest argument that premiums do not fully unwind on a diplomatic headline. EGA's own 02-Jul disclosure, carried in SMM's 31-Jul overseas review, gives the first hard public pot count: anode removal complete for all pots, pot cleaning about 90% complete, solidified aluminium cleared from over 20% of pots, and 89 of 1,262 pots back in operation - after the first repaired pot restarted on 26-May. That is roughly 7% of the potline. Alba disclosed on 15-Mar-2026 that it had initiated a controlled shutdown of Reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3, equal to 19% of its 1,623,000 t/y capacity, citing supply and transit disruption affecting the Strait of Hormuz, and on 29-Mar confirmed its facility had been subject to an Iranian attack on 28-Mar with two employees suffering minor injuries. Alba's Q1-2026 results quantified the operational cost: sales volume 312,563 t (-17% y/y) and net finished production 339,734 t (-14% y/y). Restarting a frozen potline is a months-long capital exercise, not a policy decision.
drivers.source: Alba - Q1-2026 results and 15-Mar-2026 Lines 1-3 shutdown disclosure

drivers.text: Gulf war-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value - over $7 million per transit on a $100m vessel versus 0.25% pre-war - reprices on underwriters' cycles, not on headlines, and a tanker was still struck on 01-Aug — AL Circle's 24-Jul Middle East review assembles the public picture: war-risk insurance for Gulf transits stood at roughly 0.25% of hull value before February's escalation, quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes, and by mid-July was quoted at 3-10% - the difference between a $250,000 premium and one exceeding $7 million on a single transit. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. The five GCC smelters produced about 6.16 Mt in 2025 (roughly 8% of world supply) with more than 80% exported; analysts pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of losses through 2026, near 5% of global primary supply. THE TIMING MATTERS: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by a projectile about 20 km north-east of Lima, Oman on 01-Aug - reported as an LNG carrier with Qatari cargo - with a second incident 40 km north-east of Khasab. That was the day of the cancellation, not before it. Insurance is a lagging, contractual cost; it will not fall on the announcement of talks.
drivers.source: AL Circle - 2026 Middle East aluminium outlook: 5% of global supply, USD 7 million insurance and the Hormuz effect (24-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% is $1,598.00/t of the US duty-paid premium at the 31-Jul cash - re-verified unchanged this run, and the tariff leg is flat because the metal price is flat — Aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium pay 50% ad valorem on full customs value; derivative aluminium content pays 25%. The structure originates in the April-2026 proclamation and was further adjusted by the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (Federal Register 2026-11314, effective 08-Jun-2026), whose 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window applies to the Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs - 15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally lets companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) import at half the applicable rate against expected output; no CBP guidance has been issued yet. MECHANICS: at the 31-Jul cash of $3,196.00 the 50% leg computes to $1,598.00/t exactly, unchanged from the prior compile because no new official has printed. This is the reason the US premium is not a clean scarcity signal and must not be read alongside MJP or EDU as if it were.
drivers.source: Federal Register 2026-11314 - Adjusting imports of aluminum into the United States (effective 08-Jun-2026); 20-Jul-2026 smelter-investment proclamation

notes: Alumina is roughly 1.92 t per tonne of aluminium and typically 30-40% of smelter cash cost, so it is the single largest determinant of where the industry cost curve sits and therefore of how far the metal price can fall before supply responds. That question is unusually live this run: with the weekend de-escalation pulling the metal price down, a falling alumina cost removes the floor that would otherwise force curtailment.

THE PRECISE CURRENT SMM CHINA INDEX LEVEL IS NOT PUBLISHED HERE because it sits behind SMM's paywall. The last free print of 2,730.17 yuan/mt is carried at 16-Jul-2026, and the date was deliberately NOT upgraded this run: a re-check returned the identical value against a later page date, so the index could not be confirmed as having advanced. THE MARKS ON THIS TABLE ARE OF DIFFERENT VINTAGES AND EACH ROW STATES ITS OWN. The CME futures line is the freshest and was REFRESHED THIS RUN to $333.34/t; SMM's FOB Western Australia assessment is carried at 09-Jul; the Platts FOB Australia mark at 26-Jun is stale at 38 days. Ex-China supply is two-sided: EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is ramping back after a three-and-a-half-month outage but does not expect full alumina capability until year-end (2.4 Mt in 2025, 46% of company feedstock needs), while Rio Tinto's Yarwun will be cut 40% from October 2026 on tailings constraints.

COMMERCIAL LOGIC OF A FALLING COST FLOOR: cheap alumina is a principal reason the July earnings season was uniformly strong across the producer set - Alcoa's Aluminum segment posted record EBITDA at a 32.3% margin and Hydro beat on adjusted EBITDA. It is also why a falling metal price does not immediately translate into supply discipline. Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against a 45 Mt ceiling with H1 output of 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y); with alumina near its cost floor and energy now falling too, there is no cost-side mechanism forcing that capacity out. Watch the SHFE alumina contract's test of 2,600 yuan/mt as the marker.

items.label: Calcined petroleum coke (CPC, anode-grade)
items.note: No public CPC spot print exists for July 2026; the sourceable frame is a $468-524/MT expected range for 2026 with Q1 regional marks of US $385, China $359, Brazil $450, South Korea $586. The feedstock IS dated and rising: Shandong green petcoke settled the June cycle at CNY 3,727.4/t for 3A (+30.5 MoM), 3,470.5 for 3B and 2,868.8 for 3C (published 17-Jul), which is pushing calcined costs up. Petcoke is 70.4% of prebaked anode cost. | 03-AUG UPDATE: AL Circle published a 03-Aug piece tracing the oil-to-metal chain explicitly - crude feeds green petroleum coke, which is calcined into CPC and baked into the prebaked anode, so the Middle East crisis that raised crude also raised anode costs. Brent fell 4.61% to $83.88 on 03-Aug after the Iran strike was called off. That is a cost-side RELIEF for smelters and it arrives at exactly the moment the same headline removes the supply-risk bid from the metal price - the cost floor and the price ceiling are moving down together, which is why de-escalation is not automatically margin-negative.

THIS IS THE SLOWEST-MOVING PART OF THE DELIVERED-COST STACK AND IT WILL NOT FALL ON AN ANNOUNCEMENT. Underwriters reprice on their own cycles against realised loss experience, and the most recent realised loss is the 01-Aug tanker strike near Lima, Oman - the same day as the cancellation. Even on a signed agreement, the insurance wedge is likely to persist for months, which puts a floor under Gulf-origin delivered costs independent of the LME price.

On 02-Aug the regime recorded here was 'both Gulf chokepoints impaired simultaneously'. Over the weekend Trump cancelled a planned strike on Iran, said the perimeters of a deal had been agreed and claimed the deal delivers an immediate, complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz, with talks starting Monday 03-Aug afternoon. THE CORRIDORS BELOW ARE NOT YET RE-CLASSIFIED, and that is deliberate: the announcement is not a signed agreement, a tanker was struck near Lima, Oman on 01-Aug, and no Hormuz or Bab al Mandeb transit data for 02-03 Aug has been published. flows.note: About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June. Transit has been the binding constraint rather than production - SMM says the renewed conflict has not re-stopped smelter output - but production is now also impaired in its own right: EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots on 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) shut since 15-Mar. THE WEEKEND PUTS A REOPENING ON THE TABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME, with Trump explicitly claiming an immediate and complete opening of the strait as part of the announced deal. Kept at 'tightening' pending observable transit recovery: the last published count is about ten commodity vessels on 31-Jul against more than 100 pre-war, and a tanker was struck near Lima, Oman on 01-Aug. Even a full transit reopening leaves the production impairment in place for quarters.

catalysts.text: FIRST AUGUST LME OFFICIAL, 13:20 London - and now doubly informative: the first print of the month AND the first official struck after the weekend de-escalation. Three things to read off it. (1) Does the +$17.00 cash-3M backwardation hold, rebuild or flip to contango? It has already given back 61% of its late-July widening on a demand shock; surviving a supply-risk shock as well would be the strongest evidence yet that the tightness is physical. (2) Does cash hold $3,159.50, the 28-Jul swing low and the stated short-term Elliott invalidation? (3) Does the stock draw extend a 24th session?

US-IRAN TALKS BEGIN. Trump said the perimeters of a deal had been agreed and framed it as delivering an immediate, complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Substance versus announcement is the whole question: a signed, verifiable agreement with observable transit recovery is the bear case; talks that stall leaves the supply constraint intact and the inventory position dominant.

ALBA (Aluminium Bahrain) Q2 and H1-2026 results, per its published financial calendar - the most direct Gulf-disruption read available. First producer P&L covering a full quarter with Reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) shut since 15-Mar. Q1 showed the shape: sales volume -17% y/y and net finished production -14% y/y, yet net profit rose to BHD 75.3m because the LME averaged $3,195/t, +22% y/y. Watch for any restart guidance on Lines 1-3 and the first consolidation of the $2.2bn Aluminium Dunkerque acquisition closed 02-Jun.

HORMUZ AND BAB AL MANDEB TRANSIT COUNTS - the observable that decides whether the diplomatic headline is real. Hormuz ran about ten commodity vessels on 31-Jul against more than 100 pre-war; Bab al Mandeb recovered to 31 from a weekly low of 16. No data for 02-03 Aug has been published. A recovery toward pre-war levels is the single most bearish thing that could happen to the premium complex; continued single-digit transits would tell the market the announcement changed nothing physical.

WHETHER LME STOCK BREAKS 260,000 t - the draw has run 23 consecutive published sessions without a build to 264,400 t, a fresh low this century and -48.1% year-to-date. This is the part of the bull case the weekend did not touch, and the first BUILD would be far more significant than any further draw because it would mean metal is being returned to warehouse as the risk premium unwinds.

Century Aluminum Q2-2026 results - the purest US and Section-232 read in the peer set, and the cleanest test of how much of the US Midwest premium is converting into margin now that Mt. Holly has returned to full capacity for the first time since 2015.

Hindalco Q1 FY27 results - management has already guided to roughly 5% higher aluminium costs, so the read is on whether Indian integrated economics hold up as the LME risk premium unwinds. India is the swing consumer the bull case relies on outside China.

SMM weekly China aluminium ingot and billet social inventory - the direct test of whether the sub-1 Mt destocking (953,000 t at 30-Jul, -35% from the early-May high) continues or reverses into the seasonal off-peak, with bar processing fees already down nearly 20% and extruder rates falling.

SMM alumina index and the SHFE alumina contract's test of 2,600 yuan/mt - SMM has flagged this explicitly, with the most-traded contract at 2,621 and the industry cost floor near 2,530 on Guinea bauxite at $70-75/mt. A break below 2,600 removes what is left of the cost-push argument.

Q4-2026 MJP CIF Japan premium negotiations expected to open - Q3 settled at an 11-year high of $395/t on 06-Jul and no public offers or talks coverage exists yet. The negotiating backdrop has swung against sellers in a week: de-escalation attacks the scarcity case, joint US-Japan intervention has the yen roughly 5% firmer in three sessions, and the LME backwardation has halved. Against that, Gulf physical supply is still impaired and exchange stock is at a century low.
China August PMIs and industrial output - the test of whether July's split (private RatingDog 50.9 versus official NBS 49.2) resolves upward or downward - then the 15-16 September FOMC with dots.

risks.text: THE GEOPOLITICAL SUPPLY PREMIUM IS NOW ACTIVELY UNWINDING - Trump cancelled the planned Iran strike, said the perimeters of a deal had been agreed and claimed an immediate and complete opening of the Strait of Hormuz, with talks starting 03-Aug afternoon. Brent -4.61% and Dutch TTF -4.23% on the day. The June precedent is on the official record: on the 17-Jun ceasefire the official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6%. This is the single largest risk on the board and it is the one that changed this run.

THE PROMPT PREMIUM ALREADY FAILED ONE TEST AND NOW FACES A SECOND - the cash-3M backwardation compressed from +$44.00 to +$17.00 in one session on the first official struck after China's 49.2 NBS PMI, a 61% give-back of a three-session widening run. That was a demand shock; Monday's ring is a supply-risk shock pointing the same way. A flip into contango would confirm the late-July move was a geopolitical trade rather than physical scarcity, and the flat price typically follows the spread.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING WITHOUT A DEAL AND WOULD ACCELERATE WITH ONE - outside-China daily-average output rose 1.6% month-on-month in July on Middle East and Iceland restarts, with Slovalco +75 kt from Q4-26, Marston +75 kt, Alcoa 636 kt (+5% q/q) and Balco 168 kt (+17% y/y). Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against a 45 Mt cap with H1 output 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y), and an industry margin of 6,999 yuan/mt (+56.8% y/y) removes any incentive for restraint. Cheaper energy after the de-escalation makes idled European capacity more likely to return.

THE COST FLOOR IS FALLING WITH THE PRICE - Brent -4.61% to $83.88 and TTF -4.23% to EUR 56.57/MWh cut petroleum-coke, anode and power costs; Chinese alumina at 2,621 yuan/mt on the SHFE sits only about 3.6% above SMM's stated 2,530 yuan/mt industry cost floor, with SMM warning it may break 2,600 in August against port inventory at a cycle-high 940,000 mt. Falling input costs remove the cost-push argument for defending the metal price, though they also protect smelter margins on the way down.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND IS THE WEAK LINK EVEN AS THE SURVEYS IMPROVE - aluminium bar processing fees have slumped nearly 20% as orders dry up in the seasonal off-peak, extruder operating rates are falling, and SMM attributes the ingot destocking to supply contraction and a rising liquid-aluminium share (78.3%, forecast 78.5% in August) rather than to demand pull. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 with non-manufacturing at 49.0.

A FIRMER YEN AFTER JOINT US-JAPAN INTERVENTION COMPLICATES THE Q4 PREMIUM - the first coordinated yen-buying action since 2011 has taken USD/JPY to 156.44, roughly 5% firmer in three sessions from 163.4, with Tokyo warning it will act again. It cuts both ways: cheaper dollar metal in local currency improves Japanese affordability, but it also removes an argument producers were using to justify a higher Q4-2026 CIF Japan premium off an 11-year-high $395/t base, and MJP negotiations open around late August.

EXTERNAL DEMAND IS OUTPERFORMING THE OFFICIAL CHINA SURVEY - the private RatingDog July manufacturing PMI printed 50.9, in expansion, against NBS 49.2, with new orders up a 14th month and foreign sales rising for the first time in three. Korea 53.1, Taiwan 55.1 and Vietnam 52.9 all expanded with export orders improving. This is a risk to the BEARISH case: the demand collapse the 49.2 print implied is not confirmed by any other Asian survey.

Tightening risk is DEFERRED, NOT REMOVED - the Fed held 9-3 with three dissents FOR a hike on 29-Jul and the Bank of England 6-3 on 30-Jul, with the US 10-year at 4.74%. June US core PCE at +0.1% m/m and 3.3% y/y leans dovish, and a sustained fall in oil and gas after the de-escalation would take the energy impulse out of the second-half inflation path - which on balance now points AWAY from a hike and is dollar-negative at the margin. The 15-16 September FOMC with dots is the decision point.

ANALYST PRICE TARGETS ON THIS BOARD PREDATE THE WEEKEND. Every published 2026 range quoted here, and SMM's 01-Aug weekly call of LME $3,100-3,250, was written before the strike cancellation. They are a distribution of prior views, not current guidance.
